NEW FINDING -- repository integrity, not a doc-content issue. This run discovered that `main`'s commit history before 2026-11-10T05:39:18Z is severed from the current tip. Commit `40500e21d5d694620717e20999c5c14ea1287cea` ('chore(doc-sync): check #128 - no new commits, bookkeeping only') has NO parent (confirmed: `git log --format=%P -1 40500e2...` returns empty, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor e7dbeca0185505791af0890f55a4f33f30053a2b origin/main` returns false) -- yet its file tree is byte-identical to the real check #121 commit (`e7dbeca0185505791af0890f55a4f33f30053a2b`, 2026-11-09T22:48, still fetchable by SHA from GitHub, not yet garbage-collected) except for this state file, which differs by exactly the few lines a normal check-122..127 bump would produce. In other words: at or just before check #128, something (same 'claude' GitHub App author as every other check commit here) replaced this repo's entire real git history -- every commit back to the actual root commit `cbfda97602371462a581cb99d736638caa050266` -- with a single fresh orphan commit holding an identical snapshot, then pushed it over `main`, and checks #129-169 built normally on top of that orphan root with no further damage. No file content was lost (full tree diffs e7dbeca->40500e2 and 40500e2->origin/main each touch only .doc-sync-state.json plus, in the second case, already-reviewed engineering-memory event-archive files) -- this is a lost-history/audit-trail problem, not a lost-content problem. But it means the four open PRs #59-#62 are based on commits (`cc59fc75`/`9a902e18`/`909d208a`/`b19b519e`) that are no longer reachable from `main`'s ref; they may still merge fine (GitHub resolves by object, not by ref reachability) but are at risk if those now-unreferenced objects are ever garbage-collected before a human resolves the backlog. This was not caused by this run -- it surfaced because this session's own container checkout initially carried a stale, never-freshly-fetched `origin/main` remote-tracking ref (still pointing at the pre-wipe `e7dbeca`), and investigating why that disagreed with a fresh fetch is what found this. This run did not attempt any history rewrite or force-push of its own; this update is a normal fast-forward commit on top of the real current `main` tip (`8764d51`). Recommended human action: inspect `main`'s history on GitHub directly, decide whether/how to recover or document the severed pre-2026-11-10 history, and resolve PRs #59-#62 before their base commits risk garbage collection. hermes_last_sha stays pinned below true main HEAD pending that same four-PR backlog, per every prior check's note.
